title: Revit Object Naming Implementation
purpose: Implement governed S4 naming objectives for Revit model files, families, types, worksets, views, and sheets without promoting source example strings into canonical naming vocabularies.
preconditions: The relevant S4 naming standard and controlled vocabulary are available for the object being named.
For a Revit model file, canonical root identity is resolved through SYNTAX-ISO19650-CONTAINER-001 and the project-specific token values required by TIVERIT-S4-REVIT-MODEL-FILE-NAMING-FIELDS-001.
Tool-local naming is used only where the governing S4 rule explicitly permits it.

steps.name: Classify the object before naming
actions: Identify whether the object is a Revit model file/information container, family, family type, workset, view, sheet, or other governed Revit object.
Select the applicable S4 syntax/namespace rather than deriving a new local convention.
For a model file, resolve the required project token values and their authority sources before constructing the name.
validation: The object is mapped to a governed naming class.
A Revit model file is mapped to the canonical information-container syntax rather than an invented Revit-only grammar.
No competing canonical syntax is created inside Revit.

steps.name: Apply the governed naming structure
actions: Construct the object name using the applicable governed tokens, order, delimiter, and controlled vocabulary.

For Revit model files, use the canonical seven-token root identity {proj}-{originator}-{volume/system}-{level/location}-{type}-{role}-{number}.{ext}; use SYNTAX-ACC-MODEL-FILE-001 only as an implementation/display mapping where the platform requires it.

If any required project token value lacks a governed enterprise vocabulary or project-approved code, leave the filename unresolved and request that datum instead of inventing an abbreviation or placeholder.
For worksets, apply the curator-approved discipline/function/scope structure where applicable.
Use dedicated View and Sheet standards for their detailed naming surfaces.
validation: Names are stable, searchable, and consistent with the governing S4 syntax.
Revit model filenames can be traced token-by-token to governed syntax plus project-approved values.
Names do not embed mutable status/revision into root identity unless the governing tool-local surface explicitly permits display metadata.

steps.name: Control renames and duplicates
actions: Avoid creating near-duplicate family/type names for cosmetic or project-local reasons.
Route governed renames, deprecation, and library changes through the applicable change process.
Do not treat source tables marked EXAMPLE ONLY as approved code lists.
validation: Duplicate/ambiguous names are identified for remediation.
Renames affecting governed identity are traceable.

outputs: Revit model files and objects named according to S4-governed syntax and project-approved token values
governance_notes: Source family/type/workset/view/sheet naming tables contain examples and proposed patterns; they are implementation evidence, not higher authority than S4.
Detailed view and sheet naming remains delegated to their specific instructions and governing registries.

The canonical seven-token model-file grammar is globally governed, while project code, originator, volume/system, level/location and sequence values are project-instance data unless a governed enterprise vocabulary supplies them.
A missing project token value produces an unresolved/indeterminate naming state, not permission to invent a code.

provenance.migration_note: Normalized beneath accepted S4 naming decisions; updated after STAR-T-GATE Inbox #10 to route Revit model files explicitly through the canonical seven-token container grammar and project-instance token sources without promoting example-only codes.
